meta.title: Terminal workspace
meta.description: An iTerm2-style terminal workspace in the left sidebar: one global panel with a tab strip, and every tab split into panes whose gutters drag to resize. It is not tied to a conversation — moving between them leaves your tabs and splits exactly as they were. Open it from the Terminal row in the sidebar; + adds a tab, double-click a tab title (or F2) renames it, and the split buttons in a pane header (or Command-D / Command-Shift-D; Alt+Shift+D and Alt+Shift+E elsewhere) divide that pane. Closing a pane or tab ends its shell and cannot be undone. Every pane drives a shell owned by the built-in terminal service, so processes survive tab switches and page reloads. Restarting the app ends every shell, but each pane keeps its last screen and shows it again when you reopen the panel, with a note that nothing is running: New terminal starts a fresh shell and Clear discards the saved screen. The layout and those screens live in this browser profile's localStorage.
